## Highlights
### New
- Setting up Crest is now a short walkthrough beside a live preview of the window you're building: bring tabs from another browser, choose your first Space's name, colors and icon, then add more Spaces. Close, move or file tabs in the preview and those changes carry into Crest when you start browsing. - Setup lists each Space with its Sub-Spaces and lets you add a Sub-Space to any Space before you start browsing.
### Improved
- A Space's look is now a Background and an Accent, each one color or a gradient of up to three, chosen on a color wheel with brightness and texture or taken from a palette. Crests and sidebar patterns sit under More Customization, replacing the Heraldic, Modern and Simple styles. - Dragging a Space's colors stays smooth while the window redraws to show them, in setup and in Settings. - On iPhone and iPad, tabs and folders you close, move or file in setup's preview now stay that way in Crest when you start browsing, as they do on the Mac. - Return in the command palette now searches anything that isn't an address, such as crest browser or a single word, with matching tabs, sites and history still listed below. An address such as github.com or localhost:3000 still opens, and the field completes one as you type it. - History results in the command palette now show their site's icon with a small clock badge, so results from different sites are easy to tell apart.
### Fixed
- Search provider chips in the command palette now show their text in white or black, whichever reads better on the chip's color. - Saved, pinned, reopened and imported tabs whose address holds characters such as { or [ return to the exact page they were saved at, instead of a broken search, and no longer show as moved away from their saved address. - An address you type or paste in the command palette now opens at the #section you gave it, even on a page you've visited before, and changing only the #section of the page you're on moves within that page.
---

## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 14 user-facing changes.
### New
- Collapse All Folders closes every open folder in a Space at once, nested folders included, without closing any tabs. Find it in the Space's menu, in the sidebar's menu and the View menu on Mac, and in the command palette.
### Improved
- Clear now keeps the tab you're on and archives your other open tabs. On Mac, hold Option to turn it into Clear All. Clear All Tabs, Option-Shift-Command-K, is also in the Tabs menu, the command palette and the Space's ••• menu, which is where iPhone and iPad find it. - Large folders open about twice as fast, with the folders inside them filling in just after, and a folder's preview on Mac appears without a pause even when it holds hundreds of tabs. - Folders brought in from another browser now arrive closed, nested ones included, so a large import opens to a tidy sidebar. Folders from a Crest backup keep how you left them. - On Mac, with the address bar in the sidebar, pages in Split View no longer each carry their own bar along the top: the sidebar's serves the page you're on, as it does for a single page. With the address bar on top, each page keeps its own. - Settings › Tabs now lets you choose separately what pinned tabs and saved tabs do after you close them, so saved tabs can go back to their saved URL while pinned tabs resume where you left off. Your current choice carries over to both.
### Fixed
- On iPhone and iPad, tapping a folder in the sidebar opens or closes it again instead of bringing up its preview. Holding a folder still shows the preview. - Folder icons wider than a folder, such as a computer or a group of people, now show whole in the sidebar instead of cut off at their edge. - Chromium Spaces can open devices on your local network, such as routers, NAS drives and home servers, once you turn on Crest Helper under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network, now Crest's own setting rather than one shared with other apps. A page that can't reach a local address says how to allow it instead of reporting a refused connection. - In Chromium Spaces, an http:// address you type or open now stays on HTTP, including when you reload it, instead of being switched to HTTPS. Links on pages still try HTTPS first and fall back to HTTP when a site doesn't offer it. - Files downloaded over plain HTTP in Chromium Spaces are no longer blocked outright: Crest asks whether to keep them, as it does for other risky downloads. - When you type a site without http:// or https://, Crest tries HTTPS first and opens it over HTTP if HTTPS can't reach it. Local addresses, such as nas.lan:5000 or a device name with a port, open over HTTP right away, and an address you type with https:// never falls back.
---

## Highlights
### New
- A new General setting keeps the developer toolbar from opening by itself on local pages. Shift-Command-I still shows it on any page.
### Improved
- Drag the frame around a page on any edge to move the window, as you can from the sidebar. The gap around a floating sidebar moves the window too. Borderless windows have no frame, so every click still reaches the page.
### Fixed
- Full-screen videos in the Chromium engine hide the pointer when you stop moving it, as they do in WebKit. - A page you send from a Quick Window to another Space responds to clicks and typing as soon as it appears, instead of only after you switch tabs. - A hidden sidebar slides out at the window's edge only when that window is in front. Moving the pointer over a window in the background no longer opens its sidebar and leaves it stuck open. - Screen sharing works in Slack huddles and in Slack's call test on pages that run in Chromium. As in Chrome, a site can ask to share your screen without a click of its own, and macOS still asks what to share. - Tabs take the title a page gives itself after it finishes loading. A link you open in the background with Command-click, or a page that shows “Loading…” first, no longer stays named by its address or placeholder. - Pages in Chromium that have no title of their own show the site’s name, as WebKit pages do, instead of their full address. A Chromium tab that reloads in the background keeps its title.
